title: Ayurveda Dravya Extraction
description: Intermediate JSON format for dravyas extracted from Charaka Samhita (Kaviratna translation). Each entry represents one substance with its pharmacological properties and citation.

id.description: Lowercase Sanskrit name, used as the TTL identifier. E.g., 'yava', 'mudga', 'godhuma'.

sanskrit_name.description: Sanskrit name as given in the text, preserving diacritics where known.

botanical_name.description: Latin binomial as given by Kaviratna. Null if not provided.

common_name.description: English common name as given or inferred.

category.description: Substance category from the text grouping. E.g., 'shuka-dhanya' (grains), 'shami-dhanya' (pulses), 'mamsa' (meats), 'shaka' (vegetables), 'phala' (fruits), 'harita' (greens), 'madya' (wines), 'jala' (water), 'kshira' (milk), 'dadhi' (curds), 'ghrita' (ghee), 'taila' (oils), 'ikshu' (sugarcane products).

rasa.description: Tastes. Map: sweet=madhura, sour=amla, salty/saltish=lavana, pungent=katu, bitter=tikta, astringent=kashaya.

guna.description: Qualities. Map: heavy=guru, light=laghu, cold/cooling=sheeta, hot/warm=ushna, oily/unctuous=snigdha, dry=ruksha, sharp=tikshna, etc.

veerya.description: Potency. Map: cooling/cold=sheeta, warm/hot=ushna. Null if not stated.

vipaka.description: Post-digestive effect (called 'assimilation' in Kaviratna). Map: sweet=madhura, sour=amla, pungent=katu. Null if not stated.

karma.description: Therapeutic actions in Sanskrit. Use standard terms: rasayana, deepana, pachana, anulomana, medhya, balya, vajikarana, virechana, etc. Add new ones as needed with a comment.

dosha_effects.description: Map: 'destructive of wind'=pacifies vata, 'provocative of bile'=aggravates pitta, 'destructive of phlegm'=pacifies kapha, 'enhances/increases wind'=aggravates vata, etc.

verses.description: Verse number(s) from which this entry is extracted. The superscript numbers in the text.

source_excerpt.description: The relevant passage from the Kaviratna text, verbatim (OCR cleaned). This is the evidence for the extraction.

confidence.description: Extraction confidence. 0.9+ = all properties explicitly stated. 0.7-0.9 = some inference needed (e.g., dosha effect inferred from rasa). 0.5-0.7 = significant ambiguity or OCR damage. Below 0.5 = do not extract.

notes.description: Extraction notes: ambiguities, OCR issues, translator disagreements, properties that required inference.
